articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Pretrained EfficientDet for Real-time Object Detection on Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Recently there has been a lot of demand for deep learning models that can operate on a constrained device. When it comes to the task of object detection, EfficientDet is a well-known model. In this study, we use the integer quantization technique to perform real-time object detection on a Raspberry Pi using the popular EfficientDet family. We use the pretrained models from the TensorFlow to perform object detection for a specific task and evaluate their on-device performance. We examined the models’ performance in terms of average precision and recall, IOU, speed, and model size. When working on a Raspberry Pi, we discovered that EfficientDet1 after quantization, with a moving average decay of 0.95 and a Stochastic Gradient Descent optimizer is a good choice.

articleTitle: The MUX-Based PUF Architecture for Hardware Security
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: In the world of Internet of things (IoT), Hardware security plays very important role. Hardware security is a vast area, in which Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) is apart of it. PUF works on the concept of manufacturing process variations. Designing the PUF is easy but replicating the same design is harder, so it is best suitable for generating the unique response with the random challenges. Due to uncontrolled process variation, the unique responses (output) are generated by PUF. These unique response are used as finger print of the IC's. It is difficult to access the data from IC's by unauthorized person after employing the PUF as a security primitive. Applications of PUF in the literature are True Random Number Generation, Identification, Authentication and IP protection. This paper presents, design and implementation of different MUX based PUF architectures, post implementation timing simulation and comparing the resources utilization of the Arbiter PUF, Feed-Forward PUF and Double Feed-Forward XOR Arbiter PUF on the ZYNQ 7000 FPGA board using the VIVADO 2019.1 software.

articleTitle: Analysis of Deep Learning Based Pose Estimation Techniques for Locating Landmarks on Human Body Parts
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: In the area of AI, the pose estimation become very popular. It can easily find landmarks on human body parts in small amount of time with the use of 2D image. There are various deep learning based pose estimation models available. For particular applications, each model have their own pros and cons. Here, we have discussed OpenPose, BlazePose, DeepPose and Hourglass architectures. Also, we have implemented OpenPose and BlazePose models to locate landmarks on push-up posture of human body. Detailed analysis and comparison between above-mentioned architectures have been presented for better understanding.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis for Single Person and Multi Person Pose Estimation Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Due to numerous application of Human posture application in the real world, it has recently gained a lot of attention. This paper gives a complete assessment of deep learning-based human pose estimation methods and analyses the methodology used, because deep learning can improve the performance of state-of-the-art human pose estimation methods. Pipelines for single people and multi-person are examined individually first. The Alpha pose and Open pose deep learning frameworks used in these pipelines and, are then compared and analyzed.

articleTitle: Investigation of Gaussian Apodized FBG Properties for the Analysis of Building Materials
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors are very much applicable for measuring various parameters like temperature, strain, pressure etc. among other optical sensor due to its various advantage particularly in harsh environment. FBG can also be used for monitoring of various civil structures by measuring the sensitivity of physical parameters for different building materials. In this work the reflectivity and peak power value of several building materials with respect to the grating length has been discussed by using a gaussian apodized FBG. Effect of bandwidth has also been discussed with the change of grating length. The entire research work has been carried out in Opti-grating software for designing the apodized FBG. In some applications related to sensing, sidelobe suppression is much more important along with high reflectivity and narrow bandwidth. We have considered a Gaussian apodized FBG which removes all the side lobes of the reflection spectrum. Grating length can be represented as the most important parameter to improve the reflectivity and peak power of the spectrum. It has been observed that reflectivity increases from 31.28% to 97.46% and peak power value also increases from −5.0541 dB to −0.1115 dB if we increase the grating length of the FBG from 10 mm to 40 mm. Bandwidth is found to be decreased from 0.65 nm to 0.12268 nm with increasing grating length value from 10 mm to 40 mm for all the building materials.

articleTitle: Marine Vessel Smart Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Sailing across the ocean is the core to multiple worldwide integral industries. To navigate safely, a smart monitoring system is essential. With the threats and challenges encountering marine vessels across the globe, ranging from internal vessel issues to piracy, distinct marine systems have proven to be efficient in applying supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) to avoid fatal consequences affecting crew members lives and the vessel as a whole. This paper introduces an innovative and integrated intelligent marine system that monitors the vessel effectively in terms of measuring the air quality, deep inside, controlling the temperature, detecting possible hazards due to leaks, fires, and potential collision with other vessels and marine objects. The proposed marine vessel smart monitoring system incorporates multiple sensors either separately or collectively connected, which are powered by a solar-based renewable energy source. Using photovoltaic cells, the energy from the sun will be converted to electrical energy and stored in a battery to power the distinct sensors incorporated in our system to function adequately. Such sensors will be linked together onto a uniform display platform that allows the user to read and command actions accordingly as per the situation at hand. Additionally, the proposed system will include water level monitoring, fire extinguishing, GPS-based guidance, and a simple antipiracy defense mechanism.

articleTitle: Physical Design and Implementation of Lakshya -Sub-system of Built in Self Test System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: The Integrated Circuits (IC) designed today are complex and hence require a good Physical Design strategies and optimization. Physical Design process involves placing all components including standard cell and macros inside the core area of the integrated circuit. “Lakshya” is the name given to the sub-system of the Finite State Machine (FSM) based programmable memory Built in self-test (BIST) with macro command. It is created with an intent to capture the various aspects and challenges of the VLSI design flow. It is meticulously planned to expose the real-world complexities in physical design which consists of submodules such as Microprocessor Core, Image Processor Core, Cryptography Core, Direct Memory Access Control (DMAC) Controller, Data Manipulation Core, Communication Core. The specifications of the Lakshya Sub-System include supply Voltage of 1.1V, sub-system area 4.2 square mm, Clock frequency of 833MHz, Power consumption under 600mW and Max IR drop of VDD and VSS 5%. Assumptions are initial Core Area Utilization ratio of 67.21% and Core to Die Boundary Spacing is 3um. Considering all the above specifications, physical design and implementation was carried out successfully involving Floorplanning, Power planning, Placement, Clock Tree Synthesis, Routing and Static Timing Analysis. All the steps in Physical Design significantly affect circuit timing and performance. The Physical Design and Implementation was carried out using Synopsys Design tool IC Compiler II. The technology node used was 40nm. The contribution of in built algorithms of the tool and also the skill of designer is important to optimally place and interconnect large number of Components.

articleTitle: CBTC Systems Safety Enhancement by Employing an IoT-Based Spread Spectrum Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: A novel Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC) scheme is introduced based on IoT specifications. Safety requirements of regular systems in accordance with well-known railway standards are discussed and the susceptibility of such systems against electromagnetic interferences (EMI) is investigated. An IoT-based spread spectrum method is proposed to counter the vulnerabilities of CBTC systems in order to meet railway standards. Necessary communications parameters such as CBTC data rate and spreading chip-rate are determined based on railway limitations, for instance train speed. The results of employing the proposed IoT-based scheme over Tehran Metro railway are displayed and additionally, computer simulations are performed for high-speed trains.

articleTitle: A Wi-Fi Based Smart Energy Efficient Wireless Sensor Network for Yield Prediction in Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: IoT is known to be the latest technology that combines sensing, communication and the Internet in a novel way the Internet of Things (IoT). The fundamental physical monitoring infrastructure of IoT is wireless sensor networks (WSNs). The WSNs are now widely used in Engineering, Science, Agriculture, and a variety of other fields such as Surveillance, Military Applications, and Smart Cars. One of the fields where WSN is commonly used is Precision Agriculture (PA). The Smart soil and plant monitoring is developed in this proposed work to increase crop production based on the characteristics of the soil, plant and environmental circumstances.

articleTitle: Audio Watermarking Using Modified Least Significant Bit Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: In this paper, a digital audio watermarking system based on a modified LSB Technique has been proposed. The main objective of the proposed method is to embed the watermark image in the Least Significant Bit plane without affecting the perceived quality of the original audio signal. Watermark bits are embedded throughout the signal instead of being localized to a particular set of bits. The proposed methodology for both embedding and extraction processes has resulted in an efficient technique that can be of great help for musicologists in maintaining their copyrights. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated by comparing it with the standard LSB Technique using the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) as the parameter. The watermarked audio is then subjected to certain signal processing attacks and the variations are analyzed to evaluate its robustness.

articleTitle: Comparative Study and Detailed Graphical Analysis of Equalizer, Chorus, Panning and Reverb Digital Audio Effects Using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: In recent years, professional audio processing has evolved quickly, from prevalent analog techniques to algorithms and systems for digital processing. With the development of technologies like the telephone and radio, the need for audio effects and processing are growing vigorously with time. As a result, a digital system used to create a professional audio effect processor must fulfil stringent requirements such as high-quality processing of numerous audio channels, real-time operation, stability, dependability, and scalability. Preprocessing, editing, and mixing are all part of the music production processing chain, as are digital audio effects. The aim of this Research Paper is to explain and demonstrate the generation of Audio effects via sound processing through the various graphical interpretations and detailed study using MATLAB and the average time to plot each effect was around 20–30 seconds. The audio wave used by us is a sample audio file available on the internet for audio processing. The audio file used is approximately of 4 seconds duration and has a 440Hz frequency. The amplitude vs Frequency plots of various audio effects were studied and analyzed and these effects are thus being compared on various digital signal processing parameters like the Fast Fourier Transform and Spectrogram Plot. We've also done a comparison of various important audio effects and their algorithms, which are utilised to improve or enhance sounds in every step of the music production processing chain, from generation to rendering.

articleTitle: Custom Based Obstacle Detection Using Yolo v3 for Low Flying Drones
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Low flying drones are on great demand now a days due to their vast applications in Security, Surveillance, Construction sites, Emergency Response, logistics, firefighting, Precision agriculture, Traffic monitoring, Crowd monitoring etc. The greatest advantage is that there is no risk of human life! These unmanned vehicles facilitate safe and secure inspections in complicated and dangerous environments. A fully autonomous drone needs support of various sensors such as Lidars, Radars, ultrasonic sensors, Inertial Measurement Units, Global Positioning system and cameras to detect and avoid possible obstacles in the navigation path. In this paper, we are trying to find a possible solution to detect custom based obstacles using a camera as the primary sensing element. Transfer learning is performed using a YOLO v3 deep learning network.

articleTitle: 4-Bit R-2R DAC in 18nm FinFET Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: All processors require the conversion of signals from Digital to Analog or vice versa for performing various operations. Therefore, it is crucial to have a fast and efficient Digital to Analog converter to augment the performance of the processor. This paper presents a fast, area-efficient low-power consuming design of a 4-Bit R-2R Digital to Analog Converter. The schematic and the layout of the DAC are done in 18nm FinFET technology. The functionality of the DAC is verified by performing the transient simulations. The Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) tool is used to check the functional equivalence between layout and schematic. Design Rule Check (DRC) tool is used to corroborate that the designed layout meets all the Foundry rules. Transient analysis of the Op-amp and the DAC is performed with the help of test circuits and the waveforms were observed. The power consumption of the designed DAC is observed to be 3.21489 mW for an operating frequency of 10 MHz.

articleTitle: Multimodal Biometric Authentication: Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Authentication plays an important role in applications like data security. In this paper, we propose a Biometric authentication via multimodal biometrics (MBAS) where authentication is done with fingerprint and facial features. A multi-factor authentication system brings more security and reliability. The feature vectors are extracted using a deep learning model, and the feature vectors are merged. Both face and fingerprint features are extracted via transfer learning on different CNN models, and finally feature level fusion is used to authenticate the user. Various methods are compared in order to obtain the best level of accuracy. FaceNet, InceptionResNetV2, Xception, EfficientNetB3, and ResNet50 are the pre-trained models. Google Colab is used to train them. The performance of the models is analyzed using various datasets.

articleTitle: Design of Compact 4×4 MIMO Antenna with DGS Structure for 5G mmWave Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: This Paper proposes, 4×4 MIMO system working at mm-Wave frequency for next generation wireless communication that is 5G, application. The MIMO antenna is basically design to resonate at 25GHz and offers impedance bandwidth ranging from 24.195GHz to 26.59GHz which is one of the preferable frequency for mm-Wave wireless communication under 5G. The proposed antenna uses Rogger-5880 as a dielectric substrate with loss tangent of 0.0009 at mm-Wave frequency, permittivity of 2.2 and thickness of 0.5mm respectively. MIMO antenna configuration consist of four rectangular patch antenna, fed with a microstrip line which is dog bone shape, for proper impedance matching, arranged orthogonally with respect to each other. The defected ground structure, which basically consist of square slot of 5×5 mm is introduced, that provided bandwidth enhancement of 8.9%. The gain of MIMO antenna proposed is 5.38dB with the radiation efficiency of 96%, obtained through simulation. Envelope correlation coefficient and Mean Effective Gain were the two performance metric used to analyze the performance of the proposed MIMO antenna system. The obtained for ECC is < 0.005 and MEG is <-3dB for entire operating band of 2.32GHz. The MIMO antenna, proposed can be considered as promising candidate for 5G mm-Wave communication, as it offers low ECC, required MEG better impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: Improvement of Power Quality Using Instantaneous Reactive Power Theory for Controlling Shunt Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Power quality issues related to voltage, current, and frequency variation are under major concern in the distribution system. The mitigation of these power quality issues is performed using different control algorithms. This paper, explains the design of the instantaneous reactive power theory algorithm for shunt compensator, its implementation, and analysis of power quality indices to show the improvement in power quality. The quantification is done using total harmonic distortion, power factor, and efficiency. A MATLAB Simulink model is designed for non-linear load and performance is tabulated and comparison is indicated.

articleTitle: Deep Clustering Assisted Authentication and Data Sharing Approach in Mapreduce Enabled Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Big data is the main ingredient for most of the analytical processing. The big data capture and processing can be incorporated using Map and Reduce functions in Hadoop distributed file system (HDFS) environment. The Map-Reduce functions are associated with Data nodes and Name nodes. During the data processing instructions are transferred among data nodes and name nodes. This paper discusses the secure authentication approach of interaction in Hadoop distributed environment.

articleTitle: Optimal Min-Communication and Migration Cost Algorithm based Approach for Efficient Task Migration in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: As more endeavors and organizations use cloud conditions and administrations to lessen IT costs, cloud specialist co-ops need to limit their activity cost of server farms to acquire benefits while contending with one another. In this review, a proficient virtual machine provisioning system for cloud server farm is presented. In light of cloudsim 3.0 test system, our test results have shown that the proposed provisioning component is extremely effective as far as CPU use and delivers less number of virtual machine relocations in correlation with existing provisioning instruments like LrMmt(Local Regression and Minimum Migration Time Approach). The test results show that our Task relocations into virtual machine plainly improve the correspondence cost and movement cost. This implies that these three calculations further develop the organization execution and decrease the organization utilization in cloud-edge combination figuring conditions. They likewise beat existing calculations as far as activity time by 70% overall.

articleTitle: Detection of Rumour Source on Online Social Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Digital data is spreading through online social networks (OSN) such as Facebook, Twitter, and Sino Weibo, the interesting question is to find out the influential spreaders based on user interaction. Digital data are diffused into the network based on three aspects temporal, structural and linguistic. Digital data can be separated into two forms as rumors and non-rumor data. In this paper we survey on different techniques used for automatic detection of rumors on online social network and do the comparative study. We develop a model for detection of rumours on online social network using a machine learning technique.

publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: In this paper, the design of modulo multipliers for the moduli <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({2^{4k}} + {2^{2k + 1}} - {2^{3k + 1}} - {2^k} + 1)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({2^{4k}} - {2^{3k + 1}} + {2^k} - 1)$</tex> is investigated. These moduli are useful for constructing four moduli sets with interesting properties resulting in simpler RNS to binary conversion architectures. The derived architectures of the multipliers can facilitate binary to RNS conversion as well. Hardware requirements and multiplication time are derived in tems of basic gates and ASIC implementation results are presented.

articleTitle: Tailor-Made Teller: A Hybrid Screen Reader
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: The Tailor-Made Teller (TMT) serves as a file screen reader, which enables the user to upload a file or text, to have it read aloud along with text highlights; which is relevant for students, people with learning disabilities and the visually impaired. Existing screen readers enable users to experience the Text-to-Speech functionality as an accessibility tool for web pages and on-screen text. However, the currently available systems pertain to specific operating systems and do not support various file formats for a free cost. The Tailor-made teller extracts text from various file programs and leverages the Google Text-to-Speech API to obtain an audio file, which contains the converted speech. The text from the uploaded file gets displayed on the user's screen, where the audio and text highlights run in synchrony. TMT has been tested on Image, PDF, Text and docx files of various sizes and possesses an average accuracy of 98.9%.

articleTitle: Correlating Land Surface Temperature with LULC, Vegetation Index and Topography
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Global Warming is one of the major climatic challenges. Land Surface Temperature (LST) is a manifestation of global warming and this happens due to the human activities on the earth. This work aims to correlate the LST with the Land Use Land Cover (LULC), vegetation density of the region and the elevation. The LULC and the vegetation index of the area have been derived using the optical remotely sensed images, whereas the LST is derived from the thermal images. The results of this research show that, for the given study area, the LST is not only dependent on the vegetation density and LULC, but it also has a complex relationship with the elevation of a geographic area. In other words, the LST is highest for the built-up areas, where the NDVI value is and it is least for the greener areas indicated by a higher value of the NDVI.

articleTitle: Investigation on Z-Source Inverter Topologies for Grid-Tied Solar Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Z-Source inverter (ZSI) offers a unique feature of power conversion in a single stage. In addition, ZSI also allows shoot-through states which result in improved reliability. ZSI becomes very much popular for application in renewable energy. This paper investigates different ZSI topologies for the grid-tied solar photovoltaic system. Different five ZSI topologies are compared and discussed with their salient features such as boost factor, component stress, and relative merits and demerits from the solar photovoltaic application viewpoint. Simulation of a grid-tied solar PV system of 5.4 kW based on a quasi Z-Source inverter (q-ZSI) is carried out to validate the theoretical calculations using MATLAB Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Clustering Text Documents Using High Utility Itemset Mining
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: The focus of the study in this paper is on clustering text documents using high utility itemset mining. The proposed algorithm groups two documents based on the number of high utility words which are common to both the documents. The utility of a word in a document reflects the frequency of occurrence of the word in the document. High utility words are the once having high frequency of occurrence. Utility of a word can be influenced by the section of the document to which it belongs. Each section is assigned weight depending on the importance of the section. Depending on the section to which words belong, although not frequent, they reflect the content of document better than some frequent word. Such words are given more weight so that they belong to the set of high utility words. Therefore, in this paper, the utility of a word is expressed as a function of its frequency of occurrence and the weight of the section it belongs to.

articleTitle: Simulation of Mapping Schemes as Per STD IEEE1901.2 for Power Line Carrier Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Power line carrier communication utilizes power lines as a communication channel for data transmission by superimposing carrier signals at lower energy levels onto 50/60 Hertz power signals. Power line carrier communication devices are susceptible to dynamic noise as the channel conditions vary depending on the connected loads. STD IEEE1901.2 specifies an adaptive modulation scheme to overcome the dynamic behavior of channel conditions. For the implementation of an adaptive modem meeting IEEE1901.2 requirements, knowledge of different mapping schemes is necessary. In this paper, coherent and non-coherent mapping schemes as listed in IEEE1901.2 are realized in the Simulink® environment. The performance of different mapping techniques with respect to Bit Error Rate versus signal to noise ratio is evaluated and compared with theoretical values. This information can be used for developing adaptive modem design.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Gold-Coated Plasmonic Photonic Crystal Fiber Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: The investigated paper offers a plasmonic sensor based on single core photonic crystal fiber. The sensing ability has been explored using the finite element solver in forms of wavelength and amplitude sensitivities. To realize the practical sensing approach, gold metal is circulated on the outer boundary of fiber. The highest value of sensitivities of 12,000nm/RIU and 1820 RIU<sup>-1</sup> are determined by employing the interrogation methods for wavelength and amplitude, respectively. The studied sensor geometry has potential to be applicable in refractive index detection for biochemical and for lab-on-chip integration. Keywords-Sensors, photonic crystal fiber, sensitivity, surface plasmon mode, confinement loss

articleTitle: Melodic Filtering for Indian Classical Instrumental Music
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: In this paper, various melodic noise filtering techniques viz. Adaptive Noise Cancellation, Spectral Methods and Deep Learning algorithms have been employed to filter music signals corrupted with additive Gaussian white noise. The noise reduction problem has been formulated as a filtering problem which is efficiently solved by using the LMS, NLMS and RLS methods in adaptive filtering and as a spectral problem solved using spectral subtraction and spectral gating techniques. Various performance criteria were considered to examine and analyse these methods. Results of the analysis shows that the LMS algorithm was the best based on all performance parameters. Adaptive filtering makes use of a desired signal as reference. However, without such reference signals, deep learning algorithms show better overall performance.

articleTitle: Fruit Grading to Assist Selection of Fresh Fruits
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: India produces annually 10.9 % of the total fruit production in the world accounting for the second largest fruit producer in the world. But due to sudden weather changes and various other factors, the produced fruits end up reaching customers in a damaged state. In order for the customers to buy fresh fruits without physically handling them and in order to help a section of people in particular, image classification paves a way by identifying fruits as fresh and rotten based on their physical appearance.

articleTitle: Implementation of Closed Loop V/Hz Control of Induction Motor Drive Using Tms320F28035 and Altair sT Embed
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: Induction motors are often attributed as the work horses of industries. Even though a wide variety of control techniques are available to control an induction motor, for most of the applications a simple V/Hz control is more than sufficient. This paper presents the implementation details of closed loop V/Hz control of induction motor drive which is controlled by TMS320F28035 DSP. Motor control peripherals of the DSP such as enhanced pulse width modulation module, quadrature pulse width module and analog-digital converters along with appropriate power electronic converters were employed to implement the control. The embedded C program corresponding to the control algorithm was generated using Altair sT Embed software. The experimental results indicate that the closed loop controller was able to run the induction motor according to the reference speed set by the user. A soft start capability has also been added to the control algorithm to alleviate any issues due to the high starting current.

articleTitle: The Impact of Mixed Reality in Education System-the Classroom Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: In the mysterious realm full of emerging technologies, there is a fantastic role played by Mixed Reality techniques. The blending of real and virtual worlds that allows individualized user control opportunities of the environment around user remarks the unique feature of Mixed Reality. The current work shows the effort of many researchers who have tried to explore the field of Mixed Reality in their own planned ways for the creation of Mixed Reality smart classroom. The objective is to introduce, how Mixed Reality device can act as real-time analytical tool for the teacher in a classroom to enhance the learning process of the students. The first part introduces the advent of Mixed Reality with some defined theories that are widely accepted and a glimpse of approaches done by many researchers. Later, an overview of an attempt to create a Mixed Reality classroom, two different hypotheses incorporating the same Mixed Reality tool called Lumilo were experimented with the assistance of AIED and ITS systems. Followed by the results of the hypotheses, aiming one of them to be employed in the classroom environment where both teachers and students were most benefitted. This type of environment resulted in better modes of education when compared to the existing approaches of Mixed Reality classroom.

articleTitle: Design of a Portable DF System with Simple and Compact Structure Operating at 875 Mhz GSM Band
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Circuits, Controls and Communications (CCUBE)
abstract: This paper reports a portable GSM direction finding system operating at 875 MHz frequency band with simple and compact structure. In the system, array of receiver antennas are placed together with other RF components including amplifiers, power dividers, phase comparators, an analog to digital converter and a processor unit. With help of the developed algorithm phase comparison between the receiver antenna channels is obtained and angle estimation is done. The developed algorithm was first run on a constructed system test setup that involves a digital oscilloscope connected to the receiver antennas in a laboratory environment. Later, the digital oscilloscope in the test setup was replaced with the RF components mentioned above such that a portable receiver system with compact structure was obtained. Direction finding experiments were repeated with the designed portable receiver system in the laboratory and in open space. Results show that with the designed system angle of a transmitter is found very accurately such that the maximum angle error between the estimated and the exact angle values of the transmitter antenna was found to be equal to 3.5° in the open space experiments for the transmitter antenna positioned at an angle between −60° and 60° on the horizontal plane same with the receiver antennas. Also, it is observed that the difference between the estimated and the exact angle values has an increasing trend with the exact angle absolute value. The findings indicate that the designed portable direction finding system is promising to be used for applications requiring accurate angle estimation of GSM signals.
